observations: Sewing machine head branded 'MERCURY' visible in photos 0, 1, 2, and 3.
The machine is mounted on a wooden cabinet table with a metal treadle base.
The treadle foot plate is branded 'SUMOPREMIUM' in photos 2 and 3.
Significant paint chipping and surface wear are visible on the top right of the machine head in photos 0 and 1.
A manual handwheel and treadle belt are visible, but no electric motor or power cord is seen.
No accessories or manuals are shown in the photos.

claims.evidence: Photos 0 and 1 show significant paint loss and chipping on the machine body.
No 'Made in Japan' stamp or plate is visible in the photos.
No electric motor is visible in the photos; the machine appears to be set up for manual treadle use.

claims.claim: All accessories and the original manual
claims.evidence: These items are not shown in any of the photos.

risks.risk: The machine may be seized or have internal mechanical timing issues.
risks.proof: A video of the machine successfully sewing a piece of fabric.

risks.risk: The claimed motor may be missing or non-functional.
risks.proof: A photo of the motor mounting and a video of it running under power.

risks.risk: The treadle belt or internal gears may be worn out.
risks.proof: A video showing the needle moving smoothly when the treadle is operated.

proof_requests: Video of the machine sewing fabric to prove mechanical function.
Photo of the electric motor and power cord mentioned in the text.
Photos of the manual and accessories mentioned in the text.
Photo of the manufacturer's plate showing the country of origin.
response.reason: The item is clearly a Mercury brand manual sewing machine. While the seller's claims of 'perfect condition' are contradicted by visible paint damage, and the 'motor' is not seen, it can be priced as a manual machine in fair/poor cosmetic condition.
